Subject: DPA redline: erase window & geo fallback

Jonas,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our latest redline (Aurora_DPA_Redline_v2.docx). Two items we need clarity on before we proceed:

1) Backups / snapshot retention: your current redline states backups may be retained for "administrative purposes" but doesn't define a maximum timeline for deletion after a customer erasure request. We need a concrete window and an assurance about the geographic location of those backups.

2) Geo-fallback: Aurora requires strict EU residency for PHI processing. We understand you have fallback routing for capacity reasons — can you confirm whether Redwood will allow temporary processing outside the EU and, if so, how long and under what controls? Our legal team wants explicit triggers, notification requirements, and a maximum duration.

Can you propose language we can work from? We'd prefer to avoid a long back-and-forth.

Attachments: Aurora_DPA_Redline_v2.docx (docx)

Laura / Marcus — forwarding Aurora's redline and ask. Quick take:

- Backups: infra can enforce a 30-day automated purge of snapshots post-erasure event in customer-controlled projects, but we need to be explicit about backups stored for disaster recovery and legal hold exceptions.
- Geo-fallback: runtime supports temporary cross-region failover; default is 72 hours with audit logs and automated notification. Aurora's ask may push to 7 days.

Propose we craft two redline options: (A) 30-day backup purge + 72h geo fallback with automatic notice and retrospective erasure certification; (B) 30-day purge + optional 7-day fallback but only with written approval and SLA credits.

Can you draft the redline snippets I should send back? I'll own the external thread.

-Jonas

Jonas — drafted suggested language below. Kept it pragmatic to close quickly; saved hard legal fights for carveouts. Key notes: 1) define "Backups" (snapshots, incremental storage), 2) carve out lawful hold / subpoena, 3) require notification for geo-fallback and a max default duration.

Proposed redline (recommend sending as "Redwood Proposed" to Aurora):

--- BEGIN REDLINE SNIPPET ---
Backup retention and deletion. Following an authorized deletion request from Customer, Redwood will initiate deletion of Customer Data from primary storage and replicas and will, where technically feasible, delete associated automated snapshots and backups within thirty (30) calendar days. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may retain Backup Data beyond thirty (30) days solely to comply with valid legal holds, lawful process, or to the extent required by applicable law. Redwood shall provide Customer with a certificate of deletion for Backup Data upon request.

Geo-fallback (temporary cross-border processing). In the event of unplanned capacity constraints, regional outage, or emergency operational conditions, Redwood may temporarily route processing of Customer Data to an alternate region. Redwood’s default maximum duration for such temporary cross-border processing is seventy-two (72) hours. Redwood will: (a) provide Customer with notice by email within four (4) hours of the event and daily status updates until processing returns to the agreed residency; (b) ensure that temporary processing is limited to the minimum scope necessary to restore service; and (c) delete any transient copies created outside the agreed residency within five (5) business days after normal processing resumes and provide an evidence of deletion upon Customer request.
--- END REDLINE SNIPPET ---

If Aurora pushes for 7 days, we counter with the optional extension clause:

Optional extension. A single extension to seven (7) days may be permitted only with Customer’s prior written consent and a mutually agreed SLA remedy (credit or alternative remediation) if the extension materially increases risk to Customer data residency expectations.

Marcus — infra confirms we can produce deletion certs and the 4-hour notification via our incident pipeline. Laura

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Jonas / team — thanks for the quick turn. A few points from Aurora Legal: 

1) Backups: 30 days is acceptable provided we receive a deletion certificate and a short summary of backup storage locations (EU regions) and replication partners. We also want logging that shows the snapshot deletion events for our audit for 12 months.

2) Geo-fallback: 72 hours is borderline. Our security/compliance council prefers 7 days in rare emergency scenarios. If you require a shorter default, we require (a) a formal exception process (written approval) to extend to 7 days and (b) an SLA credit if the extension is invoked without prior written approval. The language you proposed for notification and deletion evidence is good — we want the deletion certificate to include hashes/timestamps where feasible.

3) Audit logs: please confirm retention and access to API logs showing cross-region requests for 12 months; we will include this in the DPA appendix.

I'll mark up the attached and return with two small redlines — one to the geo-fallback optional extension clause and one to require 12-month audit-log retention for cross-border events.

Attachments: Aurora_DPA_Redline_v2_marked.docx

-Kyle

Subject: Re: Redwood proposed DPA redline (backup & geo-fallback) — next steps

Kyle — appreciate the clear feedback and the marked-up file. We're aligned on most items. To confirm Redwood's position in final form: 

- Backups: Redwood will delete automated snapshots/backups within thirty (30) calendar days of an authorized deletion request, except for lawful hold. Redwood will provide a deletion certificate and a summary of backup region locations and replication partners upon request. Snapshot deletion events will be logged and retained for twelve (12) months and made available via a secured audit export.

- Geo-fallback: default maximum duration is seventy-two (72) hours. A one-time extension to seven (7) days may be granted only with Customer's prior written consent; if Redwood needs to extend beyond 72 hours without prior written consent due to an emergency, Redwood will provide SLA credits equal to 5% of the monthly invoice for the affected service for the duration beyond 72 hours (subject to maximum of one such event per 12 months).

- Audit logs: Redwood will retain cross-region routing logs and deletion/audit proofs for twelve (12) months and provide access under the DPA appendix or on request for compliance audits.

If the above captures Aurora's required protections, please confirm and we'll prepare the final DPA for signature. For expediency, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope with the attachments and the executed redline.

Next actions:
1) Aurora confirm agreement on the three bullet points above (reply to this thread).
2) Redwood to send final DPA + DocuSign envelope.
3) Post-signing: Marcus will run a short proof-of-deletion test in our EU staging to validate the deletion certificate process (scheduling separate).

Thanks — look forward to closing this week.

-Jonas
